title: Field feedback pocket brief — model behavior & ops asks (Jun 2027)
body:
Purpose:
This pocket brief summarizes recurring customer feedback collected between 2027-05-01 and 2027-06-08 from conversations (CS calls, support threads, and account reviews). Goal: surface high-frequency asks and low-friction fixes that reduce operational risk and improve perception of the platform across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Topline signal (one sentence):
Customers want clearer, faster controls for model fallbacks and cost visibility, plus a small set of focused fixes to reduce tail latency and debugging pain for function-calling. These asks cut across product, runtime, and billing.

Sources & sampling notes:
- Inputs: 18 account reviews, 42 support threads flagged as "ops friction", 6 solution engineering deep dives, 12 in-product NPS follow-ups.
- Geography: 65% NA, 30% EU, 5% APAC. 
- Customer types: AI-native startup (4), mid-market SaaS (9), regulated enterprise (7).
- Confidence: medium-high for recurring themes; low for very specific model-internal asks.

Recurring themes (ranked by frequency):
1) Billing clarity and per-route unit breakdown (most frequent)
   - Ask: ability to see per-route token counts, per-model cost breakdown, and near-real-time billing alerts.
   - Impact: high visibility pain; customers pause scale decisions pending clearer unit economics.

2) Deterministic fallback controls and safe rollbacks
   - Ask: simple config to route traffic to a cheaper or older model variant on latency/cost thresholds and a one-click rollback that preserves session continuity.
   - Impact: reduces outages during model experiments; big trust win for Dedicated customers.

3) Function-calling debug tooling and streaming stability
   - Ask: replayable function-call traces, more structured error codes for failures in tool-calls, and smoother stream reconnection behavior.
   - Impact: frequent developer time sink; directly blocks production features.

4) Tail latency hotspots on mixed workloads
   - Ask: better tooling to diagnose which routes/batch-configs cause long tails and explicit guidance for batching knobs per workload.
   - Impact: intermittent user-facing slowness and missed SLOs.

5) Embeddings dedup & similarity drift alerts
   - Ask: automated duplicate detection for embedding inserts and early drift alerts when similarity distribution shifts.
   - Impact: affects retrievability and cost (re-indexing).

Representative customer quotes (anonymized):
- "We can’t make a buy/no-buy decision until we can attribute cost to the exact pipeline step — not just model X vs model Y." — mid-market search product
- "When a Canary swap fails, our session-level continuity breaks and we lose customer context. A faster rollback that preserves session state would be huge." — enterprise fintech
- "Function call errors show up as generic failures. We spend hours reconstructing the invocation to root cause." — startup building tool-enabled agents

Prioritized feature/issue compilation (short list with recommended next action):
A. Per-route billing breakdown + alerting (Priority: P0)
   - Ask summary: token-level and model-level breakdown for each API route, with threshold alerts and CSV export.
   - Suggested owner: product-hosted-api + billing eng
   - Quick win: add daily CSV export of per-route usage visible in Console (effort: S; ETA: 3 weeks).
   - Longer term: live per-minute billing view + alerting (effort: M; ETA: next quarter).

B. Canary/fallback control panel + session-preserving rollback (Priority: P0)
   - Ask summary: UI + API to declare fallback chains (primary -> cheap-variant -> regional fallback) and atomic rollback that preserves conversation KV state.
   - Suggested owner: product-console + eng-serving-runtime
   - Quick win: document an operational playbook + scriptable API examples for manual fallback (effort: XS; ETA: 2 weeks).
   - Long term: implement atomic rollback primitives in runtime (effort: L; ETA: 2 quarters).

C. Function-call replay logs + structured error taxonomy (Priority: P1)
   - Ask summary: attach full serialized inputs/outputs (redacted per policy) to traces and expose categorized failure reasons.
   - Suggested owner: observability + developer-experience
   - Quick win: surface raw tool-call payloads in Console for last 100 invocations (redaction toggle) (effort: M; ETA: 4 weeks).

D. Tail-latency triage dashboard + suggested batching presets (Priority: P1)
   - Ask summary: identify routes with >99th percentile spikes and recommend batching/timeout settings.
   - Suggested owner: optimize + serving-runtime
   - Quick win: add percentile heatmap per model-route in Console (effort: M; ETA: 6 weeks).

E. Embedding dedup detection + drift alert (Priority: P2)
   - Ask summary: auto-scan new embedding inserts for high-similarity duplicates and weekly drift signal.
   - Suggested owner: product-optimize + applied-ml
   - Quick win: create a nightly job that flags candidate duplicates in index snapshots and surface as a ticket (effort: S; ETA: 3 weeks).

Operational friction and risk flags (things that have caused account escalations):
- Noisy billing spikes from tokenization edge-cases (e.g., multi-byte payloads) — needs immediate support-runbook.
- Canary rollback that changes model architecture (e.g., fp16 vs int8 variant) causing incompatibilities in KV cache shape — needs runtime guardrails.
- Support access to raw function-call payloads raises PII risks — must be gated by redaction + audit logs.

Quick wins to reduce friction (recommended immediate actions):
1) Publish "Billing: interpreting per-route usage" short doc and add a CSV export for the billing page (owner: finance-ops + product-hosted-api).
2) Add a support playbook for manual fallback using existing routing rules; circulate to SRE/CS (owner: solutions-engineering).
3) Expose streaming reconnection debug flag (non-default) to accounts with ongoing incidents so CS can triage faster (owner: observability).

Metrics to track (so we can validate impact):
- Number of billing-related escalations per week (target: -50% in 8 weeks).
- Time-to-rollback for Canary failures (current median: ~28m; target: <10m).
- Mean time to root cause for function-call failures (current median: ~2.3h; target: <1h).
- Fraction of Dedicated customers using fallback chains (baseline: 0; target: 30% in Q3).

Proposed lightweight roadmap (6–24 weeks):
- Week 1–3: Quick docs + CSV export + manual fallback playbook (deliverables A.Quick win + B.Quick win).
- Week 4–8: Streaming reconnect debug flag + per-route percentile heatmap (deliverables C quick win + D quick win).
- Week 9–20: Console fallback UI and replay logs (deliverables B long term + C long term).
- Week 21–24+: Runtime atomic rollback primitives + live billing dashboard (deliverables B long term + A long term).

Suggested owners and handoffs:
- Product-hosted-api (lead): billing CSV, per-route views, alerting scope.
- Eng-serving-runtime (lead): atomic rollback, KV-cache compatibility checks.
- Observability (lead): function-call tracing + streaming debug flags.
- Optimize/applied-ml: embedding dedup and drift alerts.
- Customer-success: validate roadmap with 6 pilot customers and own communications.

Open questions for leadership / product review:
- Are we comfortable surfacing raw tool-call payloads under a redaction guard? Legal input required.
- What SLAs do we want to commit to for rollback speed for Dedicated customers?
- Prioritization: should billing transparency or rollback controls be the top engineering consumer?

Next steps (owner: Asha Patel):
- Schedule 30m prioritization sync with product-hosted-api and eng-serving-runtime (target: 2027-06-20).
- Create lightweight support playbook draft and circulate to SRE/solutions by 2027-06-15.
- Line up 6 pilot customers willing to trial fallback control panel prototypes (identify by 2027-06-24).

Appendix (short):
- Sample support tickets referenced: CS-1289 (billing spike due to multi-byte inputs), CS-1314 (function-call generic error, replay requested), RDW-3412 (canary rollback incident).
- Privacy note: when surfacing payloads for debug, ensure PII redaction and KMS-backed access control.

Prepared by: Asha Patel (CS lead) — contact: asha.patel@redwoodai.example
Reviewers: Elliot Morgan (Solutions Eng), Kai Nakamura (Observability), Sofia Alvarez (Product-hosted-api)

Document end.
